messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: ccache
parts:
Today I just discovered ccache

https://ccache.samba.org/

and would recommend it to anyone who tracks the git repository (including Jenkins, if we can get ccache working on 64-bit Windows). Essentially, it caches compilations so that they can be reused if the file doesn't change (even if you do make clean-all beforehand).

After installing and configuring, run it once serially so that it can cache Stan's C++ files

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ make clean-all && time make CC="ccache g++" O=3 test-models > /tmp/g++_caching.log
...
real    93m52.243s
user    87m29.122s
sys     4m58.650s

Now files are cached:
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ ccache -s
cache directory                     /home/goodrich/.ccache
cache hit (direct)                     0
cache hit (preprocessed)               0
cache miss                           158
called for link                      147
unsupported compiler option           11
files in cache                       464
cache size                         163.3 Mbytes
max cache size                       1.0 Gbytes
 
Now, you can henceforth do it in parallel much faster and with much more limited RAM spikes
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ make clean-all && time make CC="ccache g++" O=3 -j8 test-models > /tmp/g++_cached.log
...
real    11m48.354s
user    58m20.964s
sys     2m42.890s

goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ ccache -s
cache directory                     /home/goodrich/.ccache
cache hit (direct)                   145
cache hit (preprocessed)               8
cache miss                           163
called for link                      294
unsupported compiler option          417
files in cache                       456
cache size                         159.2 Mbytes
max cache size                       1.0 Gbytes

We can save a couple more minutes once I make an unrelated tweak to the lsat test. But it already takes only half the time as a parallel run without caching
goodrich@CYBERPOWERPC:/opt/stan$ make clean-all && time make CC=g++ O=3 -j8 test-models > /tmp/g++_nocached.log
...
real    23m3.460s
user    140m26.479s
sys     4m8.016s

I don't think ccache works properly with clang++ yet, but clang++ is already decently fast on test-models.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ccache
parts:
On Saturday, October 6, 2012 1:17:32 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
I used the tempfile() to overcome a problem in Rcpp, which seems do not allow me use the same name in different shared libraries.  So ideally I want that name to be unique.

Right. It would definitely be bad to have multiple shared libraries trying to call anon_model. But the question becomes can we largely avoid that in a more flexible manner. Maybe making the default model_name be paste0("anon_model_", tempfile()) and using the model_name for the class? I guess that is a problem if users want to have two models called "rats" in the same R session, but it seems like we could just require them to use different names.
But the issue here is the another tempfile() gets called by package inline to create the temporary cpp file to be compiled using R CMD SHLIB.

As far as I understand, that is not actually a problem because ccache matches on the file hash rather than the file name. So inline can randomly name the .cpp file whatever it wants, and it will still have the same hash unless the source has been changed.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ccache

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] ccache
parts:
Well, :( I made the change (add an option obfuscate_model_name in the ... argument for stan/stanc), and found that the cached object by ccache was not used. 

The reason is that function cxxfunction in package inline we used to compile C++ code is written to create a function by specifying its body, but the name of this function in C++ is the temporary file name.  For example, this is the tiny difference for the two runs of stan():

$ diff filea6be4da0a492.cpp filea6be5ac377ae.cpp
320c320
< SEXP filea6be4da0a492( ) ;
---
> SEXP filea6be5ac377ae( ) ;
325c325
< SEXP filea6be4da0a492(  ){
---
> SEXP filea6be5ac377ae(  ){


--
Jiqiang
